title: Epitome cosmografica, o compendiosa introduttione all'astronomia, geografia, & idrografia
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
publication_context: Cologne [i.e. Venice], at the request of Andrea Poletti
locator: Libro Secondo, Cap. IX 'Delle Terre Polari', pp. 265-266
role_in_essay: The textual half of Act III, including the section on the polar lands.
notes: Chapter read on the page images 2026-08-25. The Epitome carries its own short polar chapter, distinct from the much longer Atlante Veneto essay: two pages covering both poles, opening 'Delle Terre Artiche, ed Antartiche poco si puo dire, perche poco fin hora e giunto alla cognitione del Mondo'. It reports Magellan 1520, Le Maire 1616, Brouwer 1643, New Zealand 1654, Nuits 1627 and Nuova Olanda 1644 in the south, dismisses the Terra de' Papagalli as 'creduta favolosa', and gives the Arctic a single paragraph ending in a Dutch claim to have passed below the 82nd degree. The book's own index confirms the pages (Terre Artiche 265, Antartiche 265).

title: Atlante Veneto
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
publication_context: Venice; thirteen folio volumes, conceived as a continuation of the Blaeu Atlas Maior. Tomo I (1691) carries the polar section.
edition_state: Tomo I, David Rumsey copy, publication 12186
locator: Rumsey 12186.100 to .107, printed pp. 70-76, section 'Terre Polari, Artiche, ed Antartiche'; plates 12186.101 'Terre Artiche' and 12186.104 'Polo Artiche'; section closes at 12186.108 'Idrografia'
role_in_essay: The cartographic half of Act III and the publication context of the polar plates.
notes: Catalogue sequence read item by item, and all seven leaves of the polar essay have now been examined on the page images: 12186.100, .105 and .107 (printed pp. 70, 73 and 76) on 2026-08-25, and 12186.102, .103 and .106 (printed pp. 71, 72 and 74-75) on 2026-08-27 from high-resolution captures supplied by Vlad Simion, each leaf checked against the folio printed on it. A seven-page cosmographic essay in two columns with marginal headings, entirely distinct from the two-page Epitome chapter. The section is northern for five and a half of its seven pages: pp. 71-72 and 74 carry Greenland, the Norse settlements and the Danish crown's recovery attempts, then Nova Zembla, Statem Eyland, the Isola Mauritio and the Terra di Iesso, and name Snorro Storlefonio and Angrimo Giona as the authorities for the Greenland history. The southern discourse begins mid-column on p. 75 under the display heading 'TERRE AUSTRALI, OUERO ANTARTICHE' and runs to the end of the section on p. 76, p. 75 closing on the catchword 'e 60'. It opens by dividing the south in two: Nuova Guinea, Nuova Olanda, Terra di Diemens, Nuova Zelanda, Terra dello Spirito Santo and the Carpentaria are the parts of which some notice has arrived, while those that 'restano affatto incognite' are the Terre Magellaniche, 'che congetturalmente vengono disegnate d'intorno al Circolo Polare Antartico', and the Terra del Fuoco. The southern argument is therefore a page and a half long, and the verdicts on p. 76 do not rest on unread reasoning. Both poles are treated at length; only the plates are asymmetric. Rumsey's record is internally inconsistent about the date, Pub Title reading MDCXCI against a Pub Date of 1693.

title: Vincenzo Coronelli Cosmographer (1650-1718)
creator: Marica Milanesi
publication_context: Brepols, Terrarum Orbis 13; 472 pp., 44 colour illustrations; ISBN 978-2-503-56461-6
locator: Part Two, the workshop of the Frari; Part Three, Cosmografo della Serenissima and the Accademia degli Argonauti - part-level only, from the publisher's description, no page read
role_in_essay: The scholarly control on every claim Act III makes about Coronelli's method and sources.
notes: Act III's highest-priority acquisition, and still unread. Narrowed 2026-08-25: the Terre Artiche plate carries a dedication to Conte Ercole Pepoli, Senator of Bologna, so the workshop-and-patron question is now a specific one about this plate rather than a general caution. Without Milanesi the act would still risk reading a dedicated commercial plate as a personal cosmology. Bibliographic description confirmed against the publisher 2026-08-27: 472 pages, 44 colour illustrations, ISBN 978-2-503-56461-6, and the volume is in three parts. Brepols describes Part One as the manufacture of the two four-metre globes for the Galerie des glaces at Versailles and their distribution in Europe; Part Two as the workshop of the Frari, covering Coronelli's sales, his editorial work on maps, plans, atlases and an unsuccessful encyclopaedia, and how manufacture there was organised, financed and related to colleagues, competitors and clients; and Part Three as his office of Cosmografo della Serenissima and the Accademia degli Argonauti with its connections to nobility and scholarly networks. Parts Two and Three are therefore where the workshop and patronage questions should be read, and the locator records exactly that and no more: it is taken from the publisher's description, not from the book, and carries no page numbers because no page has been read. verification_state stays unverified and review_status stays candidate for the same reason; ant-gap-coronelli-milanesi does not close on a part-level pointer. One further reason to acquire the volume: the appendix is described as carrying transcripts of key documents and a list of maps attributable to Coronelli, which bears directly on ant-gap-atlante-plates and would be a better instrument for that audit than walking the Rumsey list numbers.

creator: Ernest Shackleton

creator: Frank Arthur Worsley

creator: Frank Arthur Worsley

creator: Lars Bergman and Robin G. Stuart

It reanalyses Worsley's theodolite and sextant observations from his logbook and reports a sinking position of 68 degrees 39 minutes 30 seconds south, 52 degrees 26 minutes 30 seconds west. This supersedes citing a published narrative for that coordinate, and it means the logbook is reachable through the literature rather than only through an archive visit.

short_title: Bergman and Stuart, Weddell Sea pack ice navigation
title: Navigation of the Shackleton Expedition on the Weddell Sea pack ice
creator: Lars Bergman and Robin G Stuart
role_in_essay: The transcription of Worsley's workbooks that makes the archive reachable through the literature: dated log entries, the besetment date, and the archival accession numbers of the workbooks themselves.
notes: Read in full 2026-08-27, unlike the companion Journal of Navigation paper (ant-src-bergman-stuart-location), which remains abstract-only. Gives the exact archival citation for the primary workbooks, correcting an earlier, unverified attribution to the Scott Polar Research Institute: both are at Canterbury Museum, Christchurch – "Worsley FA. 1915. Workbook for log of S.Y. Endurance from 1 August 1914 to 30 August 1915. Canterbury Museum, 2001.177.1" and "Worsley FA. 1916. Workbook for log of Endurance and James Caird from 30 August 1915 to 13 May 1916. Canterbury Museum, 2001.177.20." SPRI holds related photographic material (credited on Fig. 1: Frank Hurley, 1915, "Scott Polar Research Institute, University of Cambridge, with permission") and Worsley's later published memoirs (ant-src-worsley-endurance-1931, ant-src-worsley-boat-journey), not the workbooks themselves. The log entry for 19 January 1915 (Worsley 1915: 64) reads "Fast in pack", repeated daily until 2 February 1915 – not 18 January, which is not this paper's reading. No coordinate for the moment of besetment is given in this paper; the dated positions it does transcribe are later in the drift (24 and 27 October, 21 November 1915).
